players.product: electrical distributor - transformer buyer (HICO America customer)

quarterly_data.signal: Fourth-quarter 2025 results: record sales of $6.1 billion, up 10% year over year including 9% organic growth (approximately six points of volume and an estimated three points of price, including one point from commodities); gross margin 21.2%; adjusted EBITDA $409 million, up 10%, a 6.7% margin; adjusted EPS grew 8% to $3.40. Full year 2025: sales $23.5 billion, an increase of 8% with organic sales up 9%; adjusted EBITDA increased 2% to $1.54 billion (6.5% of sales); gross margin 21.1%, down 50 basis points on project and product mix and public power competitive pressures; adjusted EPS increased 6% to $12.91; free cash flow was only $54 million, below expectations, on higher accounts receivable and a meaningful inventory build to support growth.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 sales $6.1 billion, up 10% (9% organic); adjusted EBITDA $409 million, 6.7% margin; adjusted EPS $3.40; FY2025 sales $23.5 billion; adjusted EBITDA $1.54 billion; adjusted EPS $12.91; free cash flow $54 million

quarterly_data.signal: Data center sales set another record at $1.2 billion in the fourth quarter, up approximately 30% year over year. For full year 2025, data center sales were $4.3 billion, up approximately 50%, roughly 18% of Wesco's 2025 sales, driven by both gray space and white space with CSS delivering the majority. Gray space (critical power, electrical, mechanical, automation and MRO products sold through EES) is roughly 20% of total data center sales; white space (next-generation connectivity and IT infrastructure through CSS) is approximately 80%. Management says its capabilities now support every major phase of the data center life cycle - from power and electrical distribution infrastructure to advanced AI compute environments to on-site construction, commissioning and operations services - for hyperscale, multi-tenant, colocation and enterprise customers.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 data center sales $1.2 billion, up approximately 30%; FY2025 data center sales $4.3 billion, up approximately 50%, roughly 18% of sales; gray space roughly 20% / white space approximately 80% of data center sales

quarterly_data.signal: Record backlog, up 19% year over year at year-end, and all three business units grew backlog in Q4, which management notes runs against normal seasonality: CSS backlog up nearly 40% to a record level on data center strength, EES backlog up 6% on healthy underlying demand, and UBS (utility) backlog up 23% on investor-owned utility project activity and improving broadband trends. The CEO says the opportunity pipeline, which includes North American mega projects, is growing at a very large clip and is at an all-time record level (not sized externally).
quarterly_data.figure: total backlog up 19%; CSS backlog up nearly 40%; EES backlog up 6%; UBS backlog up 23%

quarterly_data.signal: CSS (Communications & Security Solutions) Q4 organic sales up 14% and reported sales up 16%, driven by Wesco Data Center Solutions, where sales were up over 30% on strength across the hyperscale customer base; security sales were up low double digits (mid-teens including data center-related sales) as AI-enabled data center deployments amplify demand; enterprise network infrastructure was up low single digits over the prior quarter. CSS adjusted EBITDA grew approximately 30% with a 9.1% margin, up 90 basis points. For the full year, CSS reported sales were up 18% (organic up 17%), with Wesco Data Center Solutions up over 50%.
quarterly_data.figure: CSS Q4 organic sales up 14%, reported up 16%; data center solutions sales up over 30%; adjusted EBITDA margin 9.1%; FY2025 data center solutions up over 50%

quarterly_data.signal: EES (Electrical & Electronic Solutions) Q4 reported and organic sales up 9%, the third consecutive quarter of growth in construction, industrial and OEM: construction up low double digits on strong wire and cable demand and continued infrastructure project activity, industrial up low single digits (notable strength in Canada), OEM up mid-teens. EES adjusted EBITDA grew 16% with margin expanding 50 basis points to 8.5%. Full-year EES reported sales were up 7% with organic sales up 8%, while margin fell 30 basis points on first-half project and product mix.
quarterly_data.figure: EES Q4 sales up 9%; OEM up mid-teens; adjusted EBITDA margin 8.5%; FY2025 organic sales up 8%

quarterly_data.signal: UBS (Utility & Broadband Solutions) Q4 reported and organic sales up 3%: utility grew mid-single digits on strong double-digit growth at investor-owned utilities (a third straight quarter of IOU growth - low single digits in Q2, high single digits in Q3, double digits in Q4), including grid services, offset by continued public power softness; broadband declined high single digits on a difficult comparison. The CEO says public power customers still hold excess inventory 'principally being transformers and distribution transformers', and their replenishment RFPs are 'under extreme competitive bidding pressures', which caused a significant hit to utility margins 'Specifically with respect to transformers' (a little in wire and cable; line construction materials were not affected). UBS adjusted EBITDA margin was down approximately 120 basis points; full-year UBS reported sales declined 5% (organic down 1%). Management now expects public power to return to growth only by the end of 2026, with UBS sales growth and margin expansion in 2026 carried by IOUs and grid services.
quarterly_data.figure: UBS Q4 sales up 3%; adjusted EBITDA margin down approximately 120 basis points; FY2025 UBS sales declined 5%, organic down 1%

quarterly_data.signal: Additional detail on Grid Services (within UBS; first teed up at the 2024 Investor Day): the business generated over $300 million of revenue in 2025, growing at a mid-single-digit rate for the year and double digits in Q4, built organically; management expects growth to accelerate to double digits in 2026. It supplies distribution (conduit, poles, protective equipment), medium voltage (power cable, connectivity, switching equipment including pad mount cabinets and termination kits), transmission (cable and conductor, insulators, poles and structures) and substations (high voltage apparatus, steel structures, grounding systems, power and control cables), plus program management, staging, kitting and logistics for utilities, developers and data center operators, including large load interconnects. For data centers, management describes a 'power to compute' model: UBS enables utility-side power readiness at the grid connection, EES delivers gray-space electrical infrastructure, and CSS provides white-space network infrastructure and compute-ready solutions.
quarterly_data.figure: grid services over $300 million of revenue in 2025; double-digit growth expected in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Initial full-year 2026 outlook: reported sales growth of 5% to 8% with organic sales up 4% to 7% (approximately two to five points of volume, two points of carryover pricing, a one-point FX benefit); the outlook excludes future pricing actions including tariffs. By business unit: CSS (approximately 39% of revenue) up high single digits plus with data center sales up mid-teens, EES up mid-single digits, UBS up low to mid-single digits with double-digit grid services growth and public power returning to growth by year-end. Adjusted EBITDA margin 6.6% to 7%; adjusted diluted EPS $14.50 to $16.50 (20% growth at the midpoint); free cash flow $500 million to $800 million with net working capital growing at roughly half the rate of sales; the annual dividend rises by more than 10% to $2 per share.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 reported sales growth 5% to 8%, organic 4% to 7%; data center sales up mid-teens; adjusted EBITDA margin 6.6% to 7%; adjusted EPS $14.50 to $16.50; free cash flow $500 million to $800 million

quarterly_data.signal: Near-term outlook and data center cadence: preliminary January sales per workday were up approximately 15%, with growth by business unit similar to Q4; Q1 reported sales are expected up high single digits with growth in all three business units and a higher adjusted EBITDA margin. The CFO expects data center sales dollars to be relatively consistent by quarter in 2026 against comparisons that rose through 2025. The CEO rejects the idea that data center sales have peaked ('not even remotely close to seeing a peak in the cycle for AI-driven data centers'): Wesco sees data center growth three to six quarters after the direct-ship packages of its supplier partners, which go in early in construction, customers are giving longer looks into future plans as Wesco manages their global deployments, and customer forecasts and capital spending keep rising along a 'rising power demand curve'.
quarterly_data.figure: January sales per workday up approximately 15%; Q1 reported sales up high single digits

quarterly_data.signal: Supplier price inflation: Q4 price increase notifications were up over 125% in count year over year with the average increase in the mid-single-digit range, and a higher than average number of notifications continued through January (moderating a little). Suppliers that historically took one or two increases a year are taking more, with announced increases moving from low single digits to mid-single digits. The CFO cautions that similar notifications a year earlier yielded only a 2% price benefit for full year 2025 (a point of it commodity-driven), so no future pricing is in the 2026 outlook; if the increases stick, Wesco is prepared to pass them through, with a transitory gross margin benefit.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 price increase notifications up over 125% in count; average increase in the mid-single-digit range; FY2025 price benefit 2%
